# Sound and timing

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Where picture meets the track: entries, stops, accents and effects placed so every cut lands on a sound. 10 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Micro-tick UI sound

`tx-micro-tick-ui-sound` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy any · any

(Sound) Typing and UI changes get tiny, dry ticks at or under the track, and once the track's drums run the UI goes silent, so the picture feels tactile without a loud keyboard sample.

- **Build:** In src/sync.ts emit `key` events from the same CHAR_AT array the picture types with (variant 'word' on word starts) and `tick` or `click` events on UI appearances, at weight 0.2-0.35 (12-18 dB under the landing hit), with the score's typing set to soft. Emit none of them where the track's drums run: there the hats carry the typing. When typing is fast, place one tick per word as it becomes legible rather than one per letter, and let a run of UI ticks climb about 1 dB per event into a payoff. Keep the ticks 15-20 dB A under the bed and never brighter than the music above 2 kHz (the over-bed levels in references/sound.md).
- **Timing:** Ticks 2-6 ms long, at least 60 ms (3.6 f) apart, sigma 3.5 ms timing jitter and 1 dB gain jitter either way; peaks -23 to -36 dBFS, at or under the bed's RMS; no UI sounds once the track's drums enter.
- **Use when:** Typed prompts, word-by-word builds, cold opens before the track's entry, any UI moment that wants touch without an effect announcing itself.
- **Avoid when:** Under voiceover syllables; inside a dense drum passage of the track; loud keyboard samples; a film whose idea is silent UI over the track throughout.

### Hard stop into the sign-off

`ps-silent-sign-off` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy high · launch, feature, sting

Tension rises under the back half, the music stops dead on the cut to the last line or URL, the picture all but freezes, and the lockup arrives at full speed on one hit.

- **Build:** Edit the track with an ending of `stop` (`track.py edit --end stop --gap 0.4`): the bed ends on the bar line after the body, 0.2-0.7 s of near-silence follows, then one kit element (`drop` or `hit`) lands on the frame the wordmark resolves. Choose the edit so a build in the track rises over the 3-5 s before the stop; add the kit's riser only where the track has none and nothing else leads into that bar line. On the cut to the URL or last line, hold the picture near-still (scale drift at most 0.03 %/f); the final 12-15 f before the logo sit in the gap with zero transforms. The logo move starts at full speed (its E.out curve begins on the move's first frame, with no ease-in), and the hit's 1.2-1.5 s tail covers a 90-120 f lockup hold that keeps building with a push of at least 10 %.
- **Timing:** Build 3-5 s into the stop; the bed stops on the bar line; gap 0.2-0.7 s; URL readable for at least 102 f with drift of at most 0.03 %/f; designed freeze 12-15 f inside the gap; logo move 30-68 f E.out from full speed; the hit on the wordmark's resolve frame; lockup hold 90-120 f; tail of at least 60 f.
- **Use when:** The last 4-6 s of launch films and feature reels for fast, confident brands, over a track whose last phrase can end on a bar line.
- **Avoid when:** Calm brands, where a hit reads as trailer noise (end on the track's ring-out instead), and loops with no ending.

### No low end until the reveal

`dv-held-drop` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · launch, sting

The opening plays over near silence or a light, high bed (soft high clicks on each hard step, an arpeggio with no kick and no bass), and the full-band music enters exactly on the reveal frame and stays.

- **Build:** Timeline: mute the kick and bass stems until the reveal cue and schedule a tick on every hard step before it. Anatomy: Before the drop the bed is high-passed at about 200 Hz and the ticks sit at -45 to -32 dB with centroids at 3.5-7 kHz; at the drop the RMS rises 6-7 dB and the low band goes from about 1 % to about 30 % of the energy, within one frame of the reveal. Sound: This is the sound device.
- **Timing:** The drop on the reveal frame, typically 4-6 s in.
- **Use when:** Every launch film with a construction or build-up act.
- **Avoid when:** Films that open on the product.

### Silent UI over the track

`ps-silent-ui-steady-bed` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy high · loop, feature, vertical, walkthrough

In dense, fast-changing sequences the interface makes no sound of its own, with no per-key or per-event effects, and the track carries all the energy.

- **Build:** When visible events exceed about 3 per second (multi-cell loops, speed-typed prompts, counters), emit no key or tick events for them in src/sync.ts and leave the score's typing off: the track's hats and kick carry the rhythm. Allow at most one soft tick per word or label: high-passed above 2-3 kHz, 18-24 dB under the bed, 40-80 ms decay, with 2 dB and 80 cents of seeded variation either way. Save 6-8 accent ticks per 45 s for real clicks, and put the cuts on the track's accents (MUSIC.accentNear), where the hats already sound.
- **Timing:** No per-character sounds; at most 1 tick per word; 6-8 accent ticks per 45 s; ticks 5-15 ms attack, 40-80 ms decay, 18-24 dB under the bed.
- **Use when:** Loops, grids, speed-typed prompts, counters, and any sequence with more than 3 events per second over a rhythmic track.
- **Avoid when:** Sparse, calm films where each event deserves its own tuned sound, and the payoff moment.

### The music stops for a breath before the reveal

`dv-stop-down-before-reveal` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · any

The music drops out (or dips 7-10 dB) for 0.2-0.5 s right before each big transition or reveal, and the reveal lands on the returning hit; long silences (0.65-1.75 s) can sit under holds and before reveals; a background can change on the silence; the film's only hard cut can land on a voice onset inside a drop-out.

- **Build:** Recipe: mark reveals in the timeline; the music ducker cuts the bed for 0.3 s before each. Anatomy: Drop to about -33 to -40 LUFS for 18-30 f; the hit on the reveal frame. Sound: This is the sound device: drop-out, then the hit.
- **Timing:** 12-30 f dips; silences 40-105 f.
- **Use when:** Before every big reveal; two to five times per film.
- **Avoid when:** Dips before small events (they lose their power).

### The track stops, then slams back on the cut

`ps-music-hole-slam` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Under a key statement the bed falls away for a fraction of a second (the track's own stop or break, or a short stop-down), then the music returns on the exact frame of a picture event.

- **Build:** Find the track's stops (0.15-1 s of near-silence) and breaks (a bar 5 dB or more down) in `track.py analyze`, and edit so one sits under the statement (`track.py edit`, or move the statement onto it). Either the return is the cut itself, or the statement card cuts in 3-12 f inside the hole and the next picture event (a cut, a mask click, a reveal) lands on the return downbeat within a frame. Where the track has no stop there, the effects plan's stop-down (`plan.py`: 6-12 dB for 0.3-0.5 s before a `hit` or `drop`) makes the hole and the kit's hit lands on the cut. No ducking and no suck: the hole is arrangement or a stop-down. Keep the card's own sound tiny, and use 2-4 holes per minute, the deepest before the hero cut.
- **Timing:** Hole 0.2-0.5 s for one statement, 2-4 beats for a line; the bed 6-12 dB down, or the track's own stop; the return within 1 f of a picture event; 2-4 holes per minute.
- **Use when:** Statement cards, key claims and the hero cut in a film over a rhythmic track.
- **Avoid when:** Ambient tracks with no pulse, or more than one hole every 8 bars, where it stops working as an accent.

### Whoosh run into a thud; the swap just before the kick

`dv-hit-placement` · pacing and structure · accent · energy medium · any

A series of whooshes accompanies a collapse and an exit, then a heavy thud lands on the frame the title's letters land; a word swap is placed about 90 ms before the loudest kick, so the eye gets there first.

- **Build:** Recipe: cue the thud on the landing frame from Letters' letterFrames(); the swap at kick - 5 f. Anatomy: Whoosh run about 36 f; thud +9 dB; swap 5 f before the kick at 60 fps. Sound: This is the sound device. Materials: A kick roll builds under a pull-back (five kicks at 0.09-0.18 s intervals) and a bright water-drop sound (a sine sweep 900 -> 1600 Hz over 60 ms, fast decay, a little reverb) lands exactly as the button starts to separate.
- **Materials:** A kick roll builds under a pull-back (five kicks at 0.09-0.18 s intervals) and a bright water-drop sound (a sine sweep 900 -> 1600 Hz over 60 ms, fast decay, a little reverb) lands exactly as the button starts to separate.
- **Timing:** Run 36 f; lead 5 f.
- **Use when:** Title landings; swaps on strong beats.
- **Avoid when:** Thuds without a visual landing.

### A sparse track, sound on decisive events

`ps-silence-first-sound` · pacing and structure · signature · energy calm · sting, feature, vertical, update

The track is sparse (a few notes, a soft pulse, long air) and the sound design lives in its spaces: dry ticks on decisive events, one swell under the single reveal, and effects that stop dead on the frame a key value lands while the bed rings on.

- **Build:** Choose a sparse, low-density track (solo keys, plucks, a soft pulse: low onset density in `track.py analyze`) and edit it so its quietest bars sit under the opening mechanic. Build the effects from src/sync.ts events, each tied to a decisive picture event: an opening tick cluster from frame 0 (five ticks at +0, 4, 8, 11 and 14 f), one centred tick 1-3 f after each appearance cut, a run of removals each about 2 dB louder than the last. Put the reveal on the track's entry, or on a kit swell that peaks on the first reveal; on each resolution frame (a number lands, a polarity cut) schedule nothing after the last tick, so the effects stop within a frame while the bed carries on. Close by repeating the opening cluster at the same spacing under the end, and let the lockup's single land ring over a slow push. The picture never sits still longer than 48 f; master to -16 LUFS for a piece of 8 s or less, -14 LUFS otherwise.
- **Timing:** Effects in clusters with 30-96 f of bed alone between them. Opening cluster: 5 ticks over 14 f from frame 0. Effects stop within 1 f of each resolution. Removal ticks rise about 2 dB each. Lockup hold 90-120 f after its single land, under a push of at least 10 % across the hold.
- **Use when:** Short stings and feature spots under about 15 s, calm or premium tones, number and unlock reveals, and films with fewer than about one decisive event per second.
- **Avoid when:** Dense sequences with more than about 3 visible events per second (let a rhythmic track carry them), and briefs that ask for high energy.

### Track edited to the acts

`ps-score-mapped-to-acts` · pacing and structure · signature · energy any · launch, feature

The licensed track's own arrangement tells the story's structure: its sparse intro under the hook, its first entry on the first product frame, its break under the calm act, its return for the proof, and its final hit or stop where the lockup lands.

- **Build:** Choose the track for its shape before the timeline exists (references/music.md): an intro that sounds at intent from frame 0, at least one break and one entry. Run `track.py analyze`, then `track.py edit --bars N --reveal-bar K --end button|stop|ring` so the entry after a break lands on the first product shot, the track's own break sits under the calmest act (about 5 LU down, 40-80 % into the runtime) and the final hit (button) or the stop lands where the wordmark becomes readable. `track.py grid` writes src/music.ts: build every ACT on its bars with b(), mark the act seams, the reveal and the lockup `structural: true`, and put the hard cuts inside an act on the track's accents (MUSIC.accentNear, snapToAccent) within a frame, never on every downbeat. The kit adds no drop where the track already has its entry; designed hits go only where the music has nothing.
- **Timing:** Intro 2-2.6 s, at intent from frame 0; the entry and its cut within 1 f (the picture may lead by 1-3 f); the break 2-4 bars, about 5 LU down; structural events within 1 f of the measured attack; the button or the stop on the bar line after the body.
- **Use when:** 20-60 s launch films with clear acts, over a track with an intro, a break and an entry.
- **Avoid when:** 3-6 s stings (cut to the track's last bars instead), and tracks with no break: choose another track rather than forcing the picture.

### A screen-fixed voice waveform under moving shots

`dv-hud-waveform` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · feature

A thin grey waveform with a tiny two-line caption stays fixed at the bottom centre while the camera whips and zooms underneath; its amplitude rises and falls like live audio and lies flat between phrases.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG polyline from noise(x, frame) times an envelope, placed outside the camera. Anatomy: About 60 points across, low contrast (about 30 % white), a new noise phase per frame under an amplitude envelope; outside the camera transform. Sound: It follows the voice.
- **Timing:** Active while the voice speaks, flat between.
- **Use when:** Voice and call products; a narration cue without words on screen.
- **Avoid when:** Films with captions.
